The shipped Runtime has neither (see the two defects). Records, object storage, text extraction, the ls/grep/read tools, scoping, dispatch and the model are the product's own.

The model declined most traversal requests itself (3 tool calls reached the tools out of 12 turns): the Chat tools have no direct door, so tool-level traversal handling is measured by the component probe below.

The owner's own GET /v1/conversations/:id/assets/:assetId answers 404 for a ready pipeline asset: that route reads the older transcript-reference store, so it is not a door to pipeline files for anyone (cross-scope refusal there is trivial). The refusals that carry weight are the tool and attach checks above.
The model declined to run the ten-file catastrophic grep three times; the bounded behaviour over many files is measured by the component probe.

COMPONENT probe (dist/assets/files.js and matchers.js, in-memory repository and blobs, a pass-through moderator): not the product edge, not product UAT. It exists because the Chat tools have no direct door and the model declines hostile calls.

The Studio research worker's model declined to run the catastrophic grep, so the Studio grep tool itself was not exercised on the real path. It uses the same regexMatcher (assets/matchers.ts) as Chat's grep; that matcher is measured directly by the component probe.

defects.actual: ask/chat_send create the conversation with only client_request_id. createBriefSnapshot throws 'Brief answers must be an array' (HTTP 422 brief_answer_invalid) when brief_answers is missing, even for a spec whose only field is required:false (CLI exit 0: ). With a required field the same door needs an answer the CLI/MCP has no flag/argument to supply (CLI exit 1). HTTP works with brief_answers: [] (optional) or a real answer (required). Products without a brief spec are refused by Chat itself (403 Forbidden: product.brief_spec: A Product requires a BriefSpec), so no Product is reachable by 'hatch ask' / chat_send as a first message; only --conversation/conversation_id on a conversation the HTTP door started works.
defects.repro: Publish a Product with brief_spec.fields=[{id:'goal',label:'g',required:false}]; `hatch ask hi --product <id> --wait` -> 422 brief_answer_invalid; same for MCP chat_send. Root: runtime-server/src/brief.ts createBriefSnapshot (array check) called from index.ts POST /v1/conversations; packages/hatch-cli/src/chatCommands.js startConversation sends no brief_answers

defects.title: Chat attachments cannot work on the real Runtime: no content moderator is ever configured, so every upload is refused
defects.expected: Spec (Attachments): upload first, reference by assetId, ls/grep/read answer from the file. An IM contact sending a document gets it processed.
defects.actual: A document from a Telegram contact is refused with "Uploads are unavailable: no content moderator is configured on this server.". openChatAssets() in src/chat/openChatAssets.ts builds the AssetPipeline with options.moderator ?? new UnavailableModerator(), and src/index.ts never passes a moderator (Studio's openProductAssets reads aliyunModeratorFromEnvironment; Chat does not). The same refusal answers REST uploads (see scenario 11).
defects.repro: Start the Runtime with a Postgres, POST /v1/conversations/:id/assets?name=a.txt with any bytes, or send a Telegram document to an IM Connection: 503/unavailable with 'no content moderator is configured on this server'.

defects.title: Prompts like 'Write the integers from 1 to 20' are read as a file-save request: Runs fail on web/mcp, and the Desktop is asked to write a stray file
defects.expected: An ordinary answer is delivered as the reply on every client; a local file is written only when the user asked for one
defects.actual: requestedOutputPath() (agentRuntime.ts) matches write|save|create ... to|as|at <word> and takes the word as a file path (here "20"). After the answer streams, piAgentRuntime.persistRequestedArtifact calls file_write; on web/mcp the call is refused (tool_unsupported_on_client) and the whole Run ends failed with that reason and no assistant message in history ({"mcp":{"status":"failed","reply_chars":0,"assistant_messages_in_history":0,"failure":"file_write is not available on mcp. Available on: desktop, cli."},"web":{"status":"failed","reply_chars":0,"assistant_messages_in_history":0,"failure":"file_write is not available on web. Available on: desktop, cli."}}); on desktop the client is sent file_write path=20 for the model's answer
defects.repro: POST /v1/conversations/:id/messages {content:'Write the integers from 1 to 20 separated by single spaces.', client:'mcp'} -> run.status failed, reason 'file_write is not available on mcp'

defects.title: Chat attachments cannot work on the real Runtime: every upload is refused because no content moderator is configured
defects.expected: Spec (Attachments): upload first, reference by assetId; ls, grep and paged read answer from the file, for every client.
defects.actual: POST /v1/conversations/:id/assets?name=report.md with a 300 KB markdown document returns 503 unavailable: "Uploads are unavailable: no content moderator is configured on this server.". src/chat/openChatAssets.ts constructs the AssetPipeline with options.moderator ?? new UnavailableModerator() and src/index.ts never passes a moderator, so Chat has no path to a ready asset. (Studio's openProductAssets does read aliyunModeratorFromEnvironment.)
defects.repro: Start dist/index.js with a Runtime database, create a conversation, POST any bytes to /v1/conversations/:id/assets?name=a.txt.

defects.title: hatch chat/assistant --stream crashes on the first Studio event
defects.expected: `hatch assistant <msg> --stream` and `hatch chat <product> <worker> <msg> --stream` print the reply as it arrives (the CLI help says so).
defects.actual: The CLI exits 1 with: . Studio SSE frames carry no `event:` name, so RunObserver (packages/hatch-cli/src/run.js) takes each as event "message", returns undefined for it, and stdout.write(undefined) throws. The Run itself is unaffected and completes.
defects.repro: hatch assistant "hi" --stream (any Studio worker or the Assistant, plain output, not --json)

defects.title: Chat never disconnects a stalled consumer: its limit is 160 MB per connection
defects.expected: Spec: a slow consumer is disconnected and reconnects by cursor (Studio does this at 1 MB)
defects.actual: Stalled Chat WS and SSE consumers stayed connected through every Run (4 trials, 0 closes) while 32 frames / 6142 SSE bytes piled up unread. The limit is maxSocketBufferedBytes / maxStreamBufferedBytes, default 160 MB, and index.ts refuses any configured value below MAX_RUNTIME_WEBSOCKET_PAYLOAD_BYTES (160 MB), so it cannot be lowered: each stalled consumer can hold up to 160 MB of Runtime memory before it is dropped; no realistic answer reaches it, so the 1013 / destroy path was not reachable from outside
defects.repro: run.mjs --only 6: chat_slow_consumer_trials

defects.title: Kimi prompt-cache hit rate on non-compacting turns is below the 90% target in a short conversation
defects.expected: At least 90% of prompt tokens served from cache on every non-compacting turn after the first
defects.actual: 77.5% over calls 2..N (worst call 76.6%), prompts of 5223..5350 tokens. The request prefix is byte-for-byte stable as text (tools, system prompt and history identical), so the shortfall is the provider's coarse cache boundaries (cached_tokens stop at values such as 2048 / 4096 / 4864 although the stable prefix is ~5.2k tokens) against a fixed ~5k-token system+tools prefix, not a prefix change
defects.repro: run.mjs --only 9: kv_short_per_call in results/scenario-09.json

defects.title: A whole-document summary of a long attachment is built from about 1% of its text; the middle is skipped
defects.expected: Spec (Attachments): grep and paged read answer a whole-document summary, so the answer reflects the document's beginning, middle and end.
defects.actual: A 261980-character markdown report was summarized in 3 fresh conversations; 0/3 answers named facts from all three parts. Each Run made 3 to 5 grep calls and 1 to 3 default-size reads (8,000 characters per page, 33 pages in the file) and covered about 1% of the text (see measurements.summary_trial_N.coverage); the answers describe the middle as 'repetitive logs' instead of reading it. The tool description tells the model to page until next_offset is null, but nothing makes it.
defects.repro: Upload a 260 KB markdown file with a distinct fact near the middle, ask for a six-line summary covering start, middle and end, and read the Run's grep/read calls.

defects.title: The serialized request prefix changes between calls: the newest user message is sent as a content-parts array, then as a plain string on every later call
defects.expected: A message's bytes in the request are the same on every later call, so a provider that caches by request bytes can keep the prefix (spec: the cached prefix survives)
defects.actual: Kimi's token-level cache still hit (the text is identical), but the user message at the end of each prefix is [{type:text,text}] in call N and a string in call N+1; the first raw divergence is at char 26 of 37560
defects.repro: run.mjs --only 9, then compare messages[].content of consecutive recorded requests (evidence kv_first_raw_prefix_break)

defects.title: A preempted background compaction leaves compaction.started in the journal with no terminal event
defects.expected: Spec: compaction is visible; every compaction has a durable id with compaction.started and a completed marker. A compaction aborted by a new message should leave an observable end for observers of the journal, so a `compacting` indicator can clear.
defects.actual: 3/3 preempted compactions had no compaction.completed (or any aborted marker) for their id; only the hatch_conversation_compactions claim row (ended_at) records the end.
defects.repro: Grow a Chat conversation past the trigger with a long final reply so the compaction runs after the reply, send a message while it runs, then read hatch_conversation_journal for compaction.% events: started with no matching end.

defects.title: The IM notice's dedupe key is Run id + journal cursor, not the compaction's durable id
defects.expected: Spec: every compaction has a durable id (cmp_...) which the channel layer uses for one notice per compaction.
defects.actual: Outbox source_key is compaction:run_93f596ddc1364900b87f97bcbef7db13:49:telegram::5150 while the journal compaction.started carried ['cmp_bb32478651bd4ea4a8e1b39d5cf6ee5a']. ChatGateway.progress derives the id as <runId>:<latest run.state cursor>. Exactly one notice was still sent, so this is a contract mismatch, not a duplicate.
defects.repro: Org Connection + Telegram sender; grow the conversation past the trigger; send a message while a background compaction runs; compare hatch_channel_outbox.source_key (kind notice) with the compaction.started payload.

defects.title: A cold cache with nothing to prune announces a compaction that never happens
defects.expected: compaction.started only for a compaction that runs to a result; a conversation of 131k-219k tokens with no tool results has nothing to prune and below the trigger nothing to summarize.
defects.actual: 1 compaction.started and 0 compaction.completed, with no history checkpoint. ChatCompaction.inBackground re-schedules itself after the cache TTL when tokens >= prune; ChatCompaction/CompactionStrategy.wants() then says yes for a cold cache, the job announces compaction.started, and strategy.compact finds nothing to prune and returns none.
defects.repro: HATCH_PROVIDER_CACHE_TTL_MS=2000; a Chat conversation of about 190k estimated tokens made of plain text turns; after the last reply wait a few seconds and read hatch_conversation_journal for compaction.% events.
